designCharacter: A precise instrument. Calm, dense, technical-professional: the artefact and its verdict are the loudest things present and the chrome recedes, because someone is about to trust this with a payment payload.

patterns.name: action-result-feedback
patterns.purpose: Make the outcome of a discrete action unambiguous, including when it fails, and say what to do next.
anatomy: An indication that the action is in progress.
For a failure, the reason and a way to proceed.
keyboard: The outcome is reachable by keyboard from the action that produced it.
focus: Focus is not thrown to an unrelated region when the outcome arrives.
assistive: The outcome is announced through a live region, with failure announced assertively and success politely.
responsive: The outcome remains associated with its action when the layout reflows.
prohibited: Do not leave an action in progress with no terminal outcome.
Do not report a failure without a reason.
Do not use the same presentation for success and failure.

patterns.name: export-download
patterns.purpose: Hand someone a produced artefact in a form they chose, and make clear what they received.
anatomy: A choice of form, where more than one is genuinely available.
A statement of what was delivered.
An action that produces and delivers the artefact.
keyboard: The action is reachable and operable by keyboard, and its accessible name says what will be produced rather than only naming the verb.
focus: Focus remains on the action after it completes, so a second export is possible without hunting for the control.
assistive: Completion and failure are both announced; a delivery that only changes a visual state is silent to anyone not watching.
responsive: The action remains reachable without horizontal scrolling at every supported width.
prohibited: Do not offer a form the producer cannot actually deliver.
Do not report success before the artefact exists.
Do not silently substitute a different form from the one chosen.

patterns.name: input-and-preview
patterns.purpose: Let someone describe what they want and see the consequence continuously, so the result is understood before it is committed to.
anatomy: A place to describe the desired thing.
A rendering of the current consequence of that description.
A statement of whether the current consequence is usable.
keyboard: Every control is reachable and operable by keyboard alone, in the order the visual layout implies.
focus: Focus stays where the actor put it while the preview updates; a preview refresh must never steal or reset focus.
assistive: The preview is announced as a live region so a change is noticed without sight, and it carries a text alternative describing what it depicts and whether it is usable.
responsive: The description and the preview remain simultaneously usable when they stack on a narrow viewport, and the current description survives the reflow.
prohibited: Do not clear the description when the consequence fails; the actor loses the work that caused the failure.
Do not present a stale preview as current while a new one is being computed.
Do not require a submit step to see the consequence; that turns a preview into a result.

patterns.name: progressive-disclosure
patterns.purpose: Keep a secondary set of choices available without letting it compete with the primary intent.
anatomy: A disclosure control whose current state is evident.
A primary path that works with no secondary choice made.
keyboard: The disclosure control is operable by keyboard and its expanded state is conveyed, not merely drawn.
focus: Disclosing moves focus into the disclosed region only when the actor asked for it; collapsing returns focus to the control.
assistive: The relationship between the control and the region it governs is programmatic, and the expanded state is exposed.
responsive: On a narrow viewport the secondary choices may collapse by default, and the primary path must remain complete without them.
prohibited: Do not disclose by removing the control that governs the disclosure.
Do not hide anything required to complete the primary intent.

patterns.name: validation-feedback
patterns.purpose: Tell someone precisely why what they supplied cannot be used, next to what they supplied, while it can still be corrected.
anatomy: An association between the reason and the input it concerns.
The specific reason, in the actor's terms rather than the system's.
keyboard: The reason is reachable from the input by keyboard without leaving the field.
focus: Focus is not moved away from the input when it becomes invalid; the actor is mid-correction.
assistive: The input is marked invalid programmatically and the reason is associated with it, so it is announced when the input is reached rather than only visible.
responsive: The reason stays adjacent to its input at every viewport width and is never truncated to fit.
prohibited: Do not report invalidity only on submit when it was knowable earlier.
Do not state that something is invalid without stating why.
Do not use colour as the only signal of invalidity.

journeys.name: create-and-export-artefact
journeys.purpose: The product's central outcome. Everything else ANQR offers is either a variation on producing an artefact or an inspection of one.
journeys.entryPoint: The creation surface, reached with no account and no prior state.
journeys.success: The actor holds a file that decodes to exactly what they stated.
journeys.failure: The actor is told which of their choices made the artefact unusable, keeps everything they entered, and can change that one choice.

steps.name: describe-payload
steps.objective: State what the code should carry.

steps.name: adjust-encoding
steps.objective: Change how it is encoded, without having to.

steps.name: review-artefact
steps.objective: See the real artefact and whether it will scan.

steps.name: export-artefact
steps.objective: Take it away in a chosen form.

actions.name: dismiss-failure
actions.evidence: The state returned to, with the actor's input intact.

actions.name: export-artefact
actions.evidence: The produced container bytes and their media type.

actions.name: set-error-correction
actions.evidence: The admissible join result for the changed specification.

actions.name: set-foreground-colour
actions.evidence: The admissible join result, which is where a colour pair below the contrast floor is refused.

actions.name: set-output-format
actions.evidence: The admissible join result for the changed specification.

actions.name: set-payload
actions.evidence: The validated specification the producer received.

actions.name: set-symbol-version
actions.evidence: The admissible join result, which is where a forced version too small for the payload is refused.

actions.name: toggle-encoding-options
actions.evidence: The disclosure state conveyed to assistive technology.

states.name: empty
states.feedback: What to enter, not an error. Nothing has gone wrong yet.
states.accessibleMeaning: The surface names its purpose and the input is the first stop in the focus order.

states.name: exported
states.entryCondition: The container was produced and handed over.
states.feedback: What was delivered, in what form and how large.
states.accessibleMeaning: Announced politely through a live region, with focus left on the export action.
states.recoveryRoute: Not applicable; export may simply be repeated.

states.name: exporting
states.feedback: That the export is in progress.
states.accessibleMeaning: The export action is busy and retains focus.

states.name: failed
states.feedback: The reason, which choice caused it, and what to change.
states.accessibleMeaning: Announced assertively, because a failure the actor does not notice is a failure twice.
states.recoveryRoute: Change the named choice, or dismiss and continue.

states.name: generating
states.entryCondition: A valid specification is being produced.
states.feedback: That work is in progress, without discarding the previous preview.
states.accessibleMeaning: The preview region is busy, and focus is not moved.
states.recoveryRoute: Wait, or change the input again.

states.name: input-invalid
states.entryCondition: The payload or the option combination cannot be used.
states.feedback: The specific reason, beside the input that caused it, with the input preserved.
states.accessibleMeaning: The input is marked invalid and the reason is associated with it, so it is announced on arrival.
states.recoveryRoute: Correct the payload or the option that was named.

states.name: ready
states.entryCondition: An artefact exists and decodes to the requested payload.
states.feedback: The artefact, its structure, and an explicit scan-safety verdict.
states.accessibleMeaning: The preview carries a text alternative describing what it depicts and that it is usable.
states.recoveryRoute: Not applicable; this is the state the journey aims at.

transitions.name: empty-to-generating
transitions.cause: a non-empty payload was entered and its join is admissible

transitions.name: empty-to-input-invalid
transitions.cause: the entered payload or option combination was refused

transitions.name: exported-to-generating
transitions.cause: the payload or an encoding option changed

transitions.name: exporting-to-exported
transitions.cause: the container was produced and handed over

transitions.name: failed-to-input-invalid
transitions.cause: the payload changed to one that is refused

transitions.name: failed-to-ready
transitions.cause: the failure was dismissed and a valid artefact is still held

transitions.name: generating-to-input-invalid
transitions.cause: the payload changed to one that is refused

transitions.name: generating-to-ready
transitions.cause: production returned an artefact whose decode equals the requested payload

transitions.name: input-invalid-to-generating
transitions.cause: the payload or option was corrected and the join is now admissible

transitions.name: ready-to-generating
transitions.cause: the payload or an encoding option changed

transitions.name: ready-to-input-invalid
transitions.cause: the payload or option changed to one that is refused

roles.name: content-heading
roles.governs: The name of a region, establishing the document outline.

roles.name: export-action
roles.governs: The action that produces and hands over a container.

roles.name: input-label
roles.governs: The name of an input, programmatically associated with it.

roles.name: input-surface
roles.governs: Where the actor states what the code should carry.

roles.name: option-control
roles.governs: A secondary choice governing encoding or output.

roles.name: preview-surface
roles.governs: Where the current artefact is shown, with a text alternative.

roles.name: primary-action
roles.governs: The action carrying the journey's intent.

roles.name: secondary-action
roles.governs: An action that is available but not the point.

roles.name: status-message
roles.governs: The outcome of a discrete action, announced not merely drawn.

roles.name: supporting-text
roles.governs: Text that explains a control without being an error.

roles.name: validation-message
roles.governs: Why the current input or combination cannot be used.

joinRules.name: constrains-errorCorrectionLevel-symbolVersion
joinRules.reason: Raising the error-correction level reduces the data capacity of every version, so it narrows which forced versions remain admissible for the same payload. The two choices cannot be validated independently.

joinRules.name: constrains-foregroundColour-minimumContrastRatio
joinRules.reason: The chosen colours are exactly what the contrast floor judges.

joinRules.name: constrains-payload-symbolVersion
joinRules.reason: A forced symbol version must have capacity for the payload at the chosen error-correction level. A version too small is inadmissible, not silently upgraded: upgrading would hand back an artefact of a different size from the one requested, which is a different artefact.

joinRules.name: defaults-with-symbolVersion-moduleSizePx
joinRules.reason: A larger symbol at a fixed output size yields smaller modules, so the default module size follows from the version.

neutrality.invariant: No text of a Future Use Pattern may name a product, a user-interface framework, a markup or styling language, a repository path, or a file format the pattern does not itself concern. A pattern that names its first consumer is not reusable by a second.
neutrality.reason: Reuse has to be a checkable property. A catalogue whose patterns quietly assume one product's nouns, one framework's components or one repository's layout is a catalogue with exactly one possible consumer, and nothing about its shape would reveal that.
